function: Learned ISAC transmit beamforming (ISACBeam-GNN): minimizes the 3D extended-target CRB under per-user SINR or sum-rate constraints, as a low-complexity alternative to SDR and SCA (p. 3, p. 8).
system: Downlink monostatic ISAC: BS with 8x8 UPA (64 elements), 4 single-antenna users, one 3D extended target (vehicle or drone); 3.5 GHz, 10 MHz; no RIS (p. 3, p. 10).
method: ISACBeam-GNN: graph neural network with sensing, communication and integration modules (MLP updates, mean aggregation), trained unsupervised with penalty losses on CRB and constraint violation (p. 8-10).
data_channel: Saleh-Valenzuela BS-CU channel with 100 dB path loss, pure LoS sensing path; 10240 training, 2048 validation, 2048 test samples from random user and target locations (p. 10-11).
test_conditions: Random user and target locations; one model trained on K in {299,551,875} and Nc in {3,6,9}, tested on unseen K and Nc, versus matched models (p. 11, p. 14).
baselines: Non-learned: Widebeam, MaxMin [21] and Center designs, own SDR/SCA optimization, WMMSE [34] outer bound; no learned baseline, only matched versus fixed variants of its own GNN (p. 11-14).
metrics: Weighted CRB trace of kinematic parameters, SINR, sum rate, SINR-constraint satisfaction probability, beampatterns, average computation time in seconds (p. 11-14).
complexity: ISACBeam-GNN O(max(KL, NtNcL, Nt^2 Nc)); SDR O((NcNt^2)^3.5 log2(1/eps)); runtime 0.71 s versus 49.78 s for P1.1 (Table II) (p. 7, p. 10).
openness: none; no code, data or repository link anywhere in the paper (p. 1).
q1_support: p. 10: "We utilize the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model for the BS-CU link with a path loss of 100 dB"; sensing is "a pure LoS path". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "directly evaluated across all other unseen configurations" (one model trained on K in {299, 551, 875} and Nc in {3, 6, 9}); p. 15: "zero-shot generalization capabilities across unseen numbers of CUs and ET segments".
q3_support: p. 11: "Three baselines are selected for comparison with our proposed beamforming designs" (Widebeam, MaxMin [21], Center): all optimization-based, no learned baseline; p. 14: matched and fixed models are variants of the same GNN.
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall complexity of online beamforming" by ISACBeam-GNN is O(max(KL, NtNcL, Nt^2 Nc)); Table II: average computation time 0.7135 s (learning) versus 49.7813 s (optimization) for P1.1.
q5_support: p. 11: "randomly generated based on different CU and ET locations": the samples are simulated; no code or data link is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Included: the learned method is ISACBeam-GNN (area 5, ISAC beamforming); the CRB derivation and the SDR/SCA designs are classical and serve as its reference. The BS has 64 antennas, so the single-antenna rule does not apply; no RIS (only in references). q1: custom Saleh-Valenzuela channel. q3 is 0 because no earlier learned beamformer or standard network is compared; matched and fixed models are variants of the proposed GNN.
